title: Next Greater Element (Managerial Round)
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers. For every element, find the first element to its **right** that is **strictly larger** than it. If there is none, use `-1`.

Formally, for each index `i` the answer is `a[j]` where `j` is the smallest index greater than `i` with `a[j] > a[i]`, or `-1` if no such `j` exists. Print the answers for all indices in order.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer then asked about the time and space complexity of your solution, and about the complexity of the map (hash map and ordered map) operations you rely on, followed by in-depth object-oriented design questions. State the time and space complexity of your approach and say whether a hash map is needed at all.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the next greater element of each position, in order.

examples.explanation: -2 and -5 both see 8 as the first larger value to their right. 8 is the maximum, so it gets -1. -1 is followed by 3, and 3 is last.
All values are equal, and equal is not strictly greater.
2 -> 4, 1 -> 2, the second 2 -> 4, 4 -> 5, 3 -> 5, the second 1 -> 5, then 5 and 0 have nothing larger to their right.

hints: For every index you want the nearest larger value to the right; a nested loop does it in O(n^2), which is too slow for 10^5 elements.
Keep a stack of indices still waiting for their answer, scanning from left to right.
Each element is pushed once and popped once, so the whole scan is linear. No hash map is needed.
